title: Fieldnote Insights Workshop
headline: Three ways to build Fieldnote's Insights page
intro: **3 variations of one page.** Each has a live mockup, when it is the right choice, what it costs, and a prompt that builds it. This is a made-up example that ships with the skill: Fieldnote does not exist.
axis: what the page leads with: **one number**, **a grid of numbers**, or **sentences**. The content, the sample week and the app shell are the same in all three.

blocks.title: What you asked for
bullets: An analytics page that shows people **how much they write**.
Nothing was said about which numbers, which time range, or how deep it should go, so the variations take three positions on that.

blocks.title: What Fieldnote already has
bullets: **Data:** `listNotes({ from, to })` in `src/store/notes.ts` returns each note's date, body and tags.
**Not stored:** word counts, streaks and daily totals. Every variation derives them in a new `src/insights/stats.ts`.
**Look:** the tokens in `src/ui/theme.css`. The mockups use them unchanged.
**Missing:** a chart library and a segmented control. Only variation 2 needs to build them.

blocks.title: Assumed, not asked
bullets: **Words are the measure.** Not notes, not time spent: words are the only one the data supports without guessing.
**A week is Monday to Sunday** in the reader's own time zone.
**Private.** No sharing, no comparing with other people.
**No goals or targets.** The page reports; it does not coach. Say so if that is wrong, because it would change all three.
blocks.note: If an assumption is off, say which one and ask for another round.

recommended.why: The request was to show people how much they write. Variation 1 answers that and nothing else, and it is the cheapest to build. Its `src/insights/stats.ts` is the same foundation 2 and 3 need, so starting here closes no doors.

variations.name: One number
variations.description: The page is a single figure, one sentence that reads it for you, and a quiet trend. It answers "am I writing more or less than usual?" and stops.
bestFor: People open the page for **reassurance**, not analysis.
You want it shipped in one short session.
You are not sure yet which other numbers matter.
tradeoffs: **No depth.** Nothing by tag, nothing by day.
A fourth or fifth fact has nowhere to go without redesigning the page.

variations.name: Dashboard grid
variations.description: Four headline tiles, a chart of words per period, a breakdown by tag and a day-by-day strip, with a Week, Month and Year switch. The familiar shape, and the one with the most room.
bestFor: People ask for **several different numbers**, not one.
You expect to keep adding metrics.
A date-range switch matters from day one.
tradeoffs: **Nothing leads.** The reader has to work out what the page is saying.
A new user sees mostly empty panels for their first two weeks.
Three components to build and keep: tile, switch, bars.

variations.name: Weekly letter
variations.description: The numbers arrive as three short paragraphs, written from the data, with earlier weeks folded underneath. Analytics for people who would rather read than chart.
bestFor: Fieldnote's readers are **writers**: prose suits them better than tiles.
You want the page to feel like part of the product, not an admin screen.
Looking back week by week matters more than switching ranges.
tradeoffs: **Slowest to scan.** The answer is inside a sentence.
Every sentence needs rules, edge cases and a translation.
Each new number is a new sentence to write and test.

footer: Example page shipped with the workshop-me skill. Fieldnote is fictional, and so are its files and its numbers.
